how.title: How is this calculated?
how.airspeedBody: Your GPS only knows ground speed. We cut your glides into straight {seconds}-second stretches and subtract the wind We-Fly measured while you were circling in your thermals, at that time and height. What's left is your speed through the air.
how.sinkBody: How fast you lost height on that stretch (barometer when your instrument has one, GPS otherwise). It includes the air itself going up or down: a glide through rising air looks great, one through sink looks terrible. That's why single dots are noisy and only the medians mean something. Glides that gained height are left out, so if anything your figures lean slightly pessimistic.
how.trimBody: Paragliders fly mostly hands-up or on bar, so you see clusters, not a curve. Trim is the {window}-wide speed range where most of your glides fall (the slower one, if your bar range is about as busy). Accelerated is every glide at least {excess} faster than your trim speed, usually speed bar.
how.glideBody: Median airspeed divided by median sink: what this wing would do in perfectly calm air with you on it. Your real glides vary with headwind, sinking air and wing loading.
how.leftOutBody: Turns, thermals, the first and last seconds of each glide, stretches with no reliable wind measurement nearby, climbs, and implausible speeds (below {min} or above {max}).
how.estimateBody: Wind measured in thermals is not exactly the wind on glide, and GPS has its own noise. Compare these numbers with your manufacturer's figures. This is not a certified polar. Confidence grows with the number of flights: low from 10, medium from 20, good from 40.

fingerprint.performanceTip: All values aggregate across every flight with this wing. Labels starting with “Best” or “Max” show the peak; labels starting with “Avg” show the arithmetic mean. Flights without a measurable thermal or glide phase are excluded from the relevant means so they don’t pull them down.
fingerprint.fleetTip: “Fleet avg” is the arithmetic mean of the same metric across every flight in your logbook, regardless of wing. The bar fills toward the right when this wing is above your overall baseline.
